## CFA — standardized output

```{.default}

STDYX Standardization
 ETA1 BY
   Y1                 0.712      0.031     22.97      0.000    # <1>
   Y2                 0.681      0.033     20.64      0.000

Model Fit
   CFI/TLI            0.974 / 0.963           # <2>
   RMSEA (90% CI)      0.041 (0.028, 0.053)   # <3>

```

1. Standardized loading, SE, z, p — 0.71 with p < .001 is a strong, significant indicator.
2. CFI/TLI above 0.95 indicate good incremental fit against the baseline model.
3. RMSEA below 0.05 with a tight CI indicates close fit.

## IRT · Rasch (1PL)

Discrimination is fixed at 1 for every item — only difficulty (location) varies.

```{.default}

        a      b       g
item_01 1.000  -0.842  0
item_02 1.000  0.315   0
item_03 1.000  1.204   0

M2(df) = 18.4(20), p = .560
```

1. *a* is fixed to 1 across items — that constraint is what makes it a Rasch model, not a 2PL.
2. *b* is difficulty on the θ scale; a negative *b* means low-ability respondents still answer correctly.
3. A non-significant M2 (p > .05) means the model is not rejected.

## IRT · Partial Credit Model

Ordered polytomous items — one threshold per step between categories, discrimination still fixed at 1.

```{.default}

          b1      b2      b3
item_01  -1.20   -0.05    0.98
item_02  -0.88    0.12    1.15
item_03  -0.60    0.71    0.55

```

1. Step thresholds (Andrich thresholds) increase monotonically — steps get harder as expected.
2. item_03's b2 > b3: a threshold reversal — common with sparse categories, doesn't itself mean disordered categories.

## IRT · Graded Response Model

A 2PL for ordered categories — discrimination now varies by item, thresholds model cumulative logits.

```{.default}

        a       b1      b2      b3
item_01 1.84    -1.10   -0.02   1.05
item_02 0.97    -0.75    0.30   1.40
item_03 2.21    -0.90   -0.10   0.88

```

1. *a* varies by item — item_01 discriminates more sharply between adjacent ability levels than item_02.
2. b1 < b2 < b3 within every item — GRM thresholds must stay ordered, unlike the PCM's per-category steps.

## Multilevel model

Students nested in schools — a random intercept partitions variance into within- and between-school components.

```{.default}

Random effects:
 Groups   Name        Variance
 school   (Intercept) 4.82
 Residual             15.31

ICC = 0.240

```

1. Between-school variance in the intercept — how much average outcomes differ across schools.
2. Residual (within-school, between-student) variance.
3. ICC = 4.82 / (4.82 + 15.31) — 24% of total variance sits between schools, well above the ~5% threshold where ignoring nesting would matter.
